question: Under the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court can issue ________ for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Writs.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Writs** are legal orders issued by the **Supreme Court under Article 32** and by **High Courts under Article 226.**
 
• It is used to **enforce** any of the **fundamental rights conferred by Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These writs are issued to ensure that the rights of citizens are protected and any violation of their rights is addressed promptly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are** five types of writs** that can be** issued by the Supreme Court**:

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus** is issued to ensure that a person who has been detained or arrested is produced before the court.
 
• **Mandamus** is issued to compel a public official to perform their duties.
 
• **Prohibition** is issued to prevent a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari** is issued to quash an order passed by a lower court.
 
• **Quo Warranto** is issued to enquire into the legality of a person holding a public office.
 
 
 
• **Ordinances** are similar to laws, except that they are **issued by the President of India** when the **Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, or both are not in session.**
 
• **Article 123** deals with the **ordinance-making power of the President.**
 
• **Article 213** deals with the **ordinance-making power of the Governor.**
